'''Riivo Sinijärv''' (born 27 May 1947<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.riigikogu.ee/public/Riigikogu/kogumik.pdf |format=PDF |title=Riigikogu VII, VIII ja IX koosseis |trans-title=Composition of Parliaments VII, VIII and IX |language=Estonian |page=87 |publisher=The Parliament of Estonia |year=2004 |accessdate=13 December 2010}}</ref> in [[Tallinn]]) is an [[Estonia]]n politician and a former [[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Estonia)|Minister of Foreign Affairs]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.vm.ee/?q=node/4078 |title=Ministry of Foreign Affairs 1991-2006 |publisher=Estonian Ministry of Foreign Affairs |date=15 September 2008 |accessdate=13 December 2010 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120318223017/http://www.vm.ee/?q=node%2F4078 |archivedate=18 March 2012 }}</ref>

Sinijärv is the father of poet and journalist [[Karl Martin Sinijärv]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.kroonika.ee/artiklid/1738/riivo_sinijarv_teab_elu_motet.html?art_magaz=13 |title=Riivo Sinijärv teab elu mõtet |trans-title=Riivo Sinijärv knows the meaning of life |language=Estonian |work=Kroonika |date=27 February 2006 |first=Paavo |last=Kangur |accessdate=13 December 2010 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20111006155932/http://www.kroonika.ee/artiklid/1738/riivo_sinijarv_teab_elu_motet.html?art_magaz=13 |archivedate=6 October 2011 }}</ref>
